inicio.kicker: LOOP-R Engineering Track · course 3 of 6 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Multi-agent and Orchestration: more agents only when the work pays for the team
inicio.lead: When not to open a second agent, a subagent that returns little, fan-out with a cap, separate generator and evaluator, worktree and sandbox per role, a queue that resumes without colliding, and the Claude + Codex team. Each practice has a rehearsal that doesn't spend quota and real terminal output.
inicio.capa_alt: Dark workbench with three terminal boxes connected by cables to a central box with a dial.

cursos.sub: This is course 3. Each lesson points to the course that owns the topic. Suggested order: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.

itens.l: The five pieces, the harness, the loop engines, LOOP-R, done criterion from 0 to 4, and caps.
Separate, skeptical evaluator, frozen tests, reward hacking, gold set, and calibrated judge.
The seven-file kit, goal.md level 3+, context in bands, handoff, headless loop, and measurement.
When not to use it, subagents, generator × evaluator, worktrees, queues, and the Claude + Codex team.
Lethal trifecta, Rule of Two, injection through read content, guard hooks, and sandbox.
A hypothesis with a number, an experiment, a promotion and a rollback, lessons learned, and the risk of optimizing against the meter.

inicio.aulas_sub: In the order you build a team: decide whether you need one, delegate, parallelize, verify, isolate, queue, route, and design your own.

itens: You already use Claude Code or Codex in the terminal and want to split work between agents without paying double for nothing.
You've seen two agents overwrite each other, or a queue run the same task twice.
You want Claude doing the work and Codex checking it, each in the right role.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Choose between a single agent, sequential, parallel, or hybrid using a matrix of signals.
Write read-only subagents with short returns and run fan-out with a cap per item.
Separate generator and evaluator, give a worktree to whoever writes and a sandbox to whoever reviews.
Resume queues without collisions and design the time.md for your loop, checked by a script.

Linux with git, bash, Python 3, and Node 20+ (on macOS, the rehearsals need xargs -d, flock, and timeout: install coreutils, findutils, and flock through Homebrew); Claude Code and Codex CLI signed in through your subscription.
The rehearsals use a fake agent and don't spend quota. The course's real calls (lessons 2, 3, 4, 7, and 8) are small.
Recommended: courses 0 (Base), 1 (Verification), and 2 (Long runs) of the track.
